subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [3:694] “Bodily injury” exclusion: D&O policies typically contain an exclusion for bodily injury. (E.g., “This policy does not cover … loss arising out of claims for bodily injury, sickness, disease, death or emotional distress.”) Employment-related claims alleging physical or emotional injury would appear to be subject to this exclusion. (1) [3:695] Emotional distress also excluded: Claims for emotional distress are not covered under liability insurance where the underlying acts are not covered: “Any damages flowing from noncovered losses that may lead to emotional distress cannot be used to expand coverage where none was intended or bargained for by the parties.” [Waller v. Truck Ins. Exch., Inc. (1995) 11 C4th 1, 16, 44 CR2d 370, 376] c. [3:696] “Intentional injury” exclusion: D&O policies typically do not include an express “intentional injury” exclusion. Nonetheless, Ins.C. § 533 bars indemnification for “loss resulting from the wilful act of the insured” (see ¶ 3:105 ff.).
